thread:
cust-success-jen: heads up — Acme (tenant acme-corp) reporting p99 spikes for API in EU since ~08:00 UTC, p99 ~2.4s, p95 ~700ms, occasional 500s. They suspect regression after a routing change. Can SRE take? :eyes:

alex: on it. can you paste a sample request-id + customer timestamp?

cust-success-jen: request_id=01GZ7X9QK2A0, customer timestamp=2026-03-17T08:11:12Z. They attached logs showing backend processing ~1.2s but frontend observed longer times.

maria: running active probe from eu-west probe -> api.endpoints.redwood.test. curl with timing:
```
$ curl -w '%{time_starttransfer} %{time_connect} %{time_appconnect}\n' -o /dev/null -s https://api.endpoints.redwood.test/health
0.62 0.13 0.38
```

maria: time_appconnect=0.38s looks high for TLS handshake from EU probe. repeating from another eu POP...

vikram: running traceroute from eu-pop-3 to customer egress IP:
```
1  10.0.0.1  0.5 ms
2  100.64.1.1  1.0 ms
3  * * *
4  198.51.100.23  25.7 ms  (us-east hop)
```

vikram: interesting — some ASNs are being handed off to a us-east path (cross-region) instead of staying in eu-west, causing extra RTT and TLS cost.

sre-bot: alert: high_p99_eu_api (tenant=acme-corp) fired at 2026-03-17T08:07Z — p99 above 1.2s for 15m.

network-oncall: checking GSLB+DNS decision logs for acme-corp. seeing mixed geo-weights: eu-west and us-east both eligible, but a subset of client IPs are resolving to us-east due to stale EDNS mappings. Also observed DNS TTL of 5s recently changed from 60s.

maria: dig +short from a handful of probes shows two A records with different AS path lengths. sample:
```
$ dig @8.8.8.8 api.acme-cust.redwood.test +short
52.210.12.34  (eu-west)
3.17.45.66  (us-east)
```

maria: and TLS logs show extra retransmits on the us-east path: SNI->server 3-way + 1 retransmit in ~10% of sessions. that explains the 200–400ms added to connect.

alex: hypothesis: recent GSLB roll decreased eu weight for fallback behavior and TTL drop causes rapid churning; some client resolvers pick up us-east and we get cross-region TLS overhead.

alex: mitigation plan — 1) pin acme tenant routing to eu-west for 1h, 2) raise DNS TTL to 60s for their zone, 3) monitor p99 and rollback if noise.

infra-deploy-bot: applying routing change: pin tenant=acme-corp -> region=eu-west, change_id=rc-20260317-09, owner=alex.

network-oncall: updating DNS config: set TTL=60s for acme-cust zone, propagating. note: may take ~1-2 TTL windows for effect.

maria: quick follow-up probes after pinning:
```
$ curl -w '%{time_starttransfer} %{time_connect} %{time_appconnect}\n' -o /dev/null -s https://api.acme-cust.redwood.test/health
0.46 0.11 0.18
```

maria: p99 sampled down to ~1.0–1.2s in our traces, p95 ~420ms.

cust-success-jen: customer reports perceived improvement — success message from their SRE: "latency looks back to normal, thanks" :tada:

vikram: leaving a follow-up action: create a short postmortem if p99 stays improved; recommend GSLB weight audit and revert the aggressive TTL change in the rollout that triggered this. filing infra ticket INF-4021.

alex: agreed. temporary pin will remain for 1h, then we'll A/B test weight change with smaller TTL delta.

maria: final note: added a per-tenant fallback rule to avoid cross-region handoff for sessions with TLS handshake retransmits >5%. will watch for side effects.

sre-bot: alert resolved: high_p99_eu_api (tenant=acme-corp) resolved at 2026-03-17T08:28Z.

cust-success-jen: filing closure with customer, will keep them updated. thanks all. :heart:
